name: Airtable
tagline: Spreadsheet-like database for teams, forms, automations, and interfaces

pricing.notes: Official pricing/support checked 2026-07-30; Team listed at $24/collaborator/month monthly and $20 annually.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: 1,000 records/base; 1 GB attachments/base; 1,000 API calls/workspace/month; 500 AI credits/editor/month.

tiers.name: Team
tiers.limits: 50,000 records/base; 20 GB attachments/base; 100,000 API calls/workspace/month; 15,000 AI credits per billable collaborator; 1-year history.

tiers.name: Business
tiers.limits: 125,000 records/base; 100 GB attachments/base; unlimited API calls subject to rate limits; 20,000 AI credits per billable collaborator; 1-year history.
tiers.notes: Available to organizations with a private email domain.

tiers.name: Enterprise Scale
tiers.limits: 500,000+ records/base; 1 TB attachments/base; unlimited API calls subject to rate limits; 25,000 AI credits per billable collaborator.

pricing.freeTierCaps: 1,000 records/base, 1 GB attachments/base, 1,000 API calls/workspace/month and 500 AI credits/editor/month
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual; prices are per billable collaborator and annual figures are effective monthly rates
pricing.hiddenCosts: Billing is per workspace and seat: Team can bill commenters and above, while Business generally bills editors and above. Added seats are prorated, so a user in multiple paid workspaces can create multiple charges.

verdictSummary: A spreadsheet database CRUD app is buildable, but Airtable's views, permissions, automations, interfaces, forms, sync, and integrations are broad.
coreLoopDIY: Create tables/fields/views, forms, simple automations, filters, and a REST API over Postgres/SQLite.
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay because non-engineers can turn data into workflows without asking for a custom app.

priorArt.name: NocoDB
priorArt.desc: Open-source Airtable-like no-code database built on existing SQL databases.

alternatives.name: Airtable Free
alternatives.desc: The obvious escape hatch is staying put: five editors and 1,000 records per base, with forms, interfaces, and small automations.

facts.install: Hosted signup; optional macOS or Windows desktop client
facts.engines: Airtable Omni/AI is available only subject to plan/workspace settings; underlying models are not specified for the Free alternative
facts.dataFormat: Bases and attachments live in Airtable's cloud; each table/view can be exported as CSV, but there is no single-file full-base export
facts.gapVsPaid: It is the same product with strict record, attachment, automation, revision-history, and advanced-interface limits that a paid Airtable base can quickly exceed.

alternatives.name: Baserow Free
alternatives.desc: Airtable with fewer ornaments: 3,000 rows, forms, views, automations, and a small app builder for $0.

facts.dataFormat: Tables, application definitions, uploads, and workspace metadata live in Baserow Cloud; tables can be exported as CSV
facts.gapVsPaid: Baserow has a much smaller integration, automation, extension, and polished Interface Designer ecosystem than Airtable.

alternatives.name: Fibery Free
alternatives.desc: A less spreadsheet-shaped Airtable replacement with relational databases, forms, views, formulas, and 250 automations for ten people.

facts.engines: Fibery AI is vendor-managed; the free plan includes limited AI/automation credits, but Fibery does not publish a fixed underlying model list for the free plan
facts.dataFormat: Workspace databases, documents, whiteboards, and files live in Fibery's cloud; a full-space export produces Markdown, CSV, and file folders
facts.gapVsPaid: Fibery is less spreadsheet-like and has a steeper data-modeling learning curve, with weaker public forms and lightweight interface building than Airtable.

alternatives.name: SeaTable Free
alternatives.desc: A serious grid with 10,000 rows, forms, automations, scripts, and an app builder before it asks for money.

facts.dataFormat: Bases live in SeaTable Cloud and can be exported as proprietary .dtable containers containing JSON plus an asset folder; individual tables or views export to XLSX
facts.gapVsPaid: SeaTable's interface and integration ecosystem is less polished and broad than Airtable's, especially for teams relying on marketplace extensions and automations.

alternatives.name: Teable Free
alternatives.desc: An Airtable-shaped database with 1,000 rows, 100 automations, and a real app builder on the free plan.

facts.engines: Vendor-hosted AI and App Builder features use Teable's configured model services and free-plan credits; the exact model roster can change
facts.dataFormat: Bases, records, attachments, automation state, and app definitions live in Teable Cloud; bases can be backed up as .tea files and tables exported as CSV
facts.gapVsPaid: Teable closely matches the grid, but its integrations, automations, extensions, and polished interfaces remain notably less mature than Airtable's.

rejectedAlternatives.name: NocoDB Community
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The grid and forms are real; Airtable-style automations and interfaces are not in the free Community product.

notes: Foundational page: a lot of subscriptions are secretly Airtable-shaped.
prompt:
Build me a personal spreadsheet-database to replace Airtable. Requirements:

- Local web app: Node + Express + better-sqlite3, one database file at
  data/base.db; the grid is Tabulator plus vanilla JS, no build step.
- Create tables and columns from the UI, typed as text, number, date,
  select, checkbox, or URL; each is a real SQLite table so other tools can
  query it.
- Inline grid editing, click-to-sort, per-column filters.
- Saved views: name + filters + sort + hidden columns, stored in a views
  table and listed in a sidebar.
- Link columns: a cell can reference rows in another table, picked from a
  dropdown, rendered as chips that click through to the linked row.
- A quick-entry form page per table at /form/<table>: one input per column,
  posts a row.
- CSV import and export per table so nothing is ever trapped.
- Localhost only, no accounts, no telemetry.
- Out of scope: multi-user permissions, automations, and hosted interfaces;
  when teammates need in, that is what Airtable is for.
- README: setup and where the database lives.
